name: Eleusis
description: Eleusis is a groundbreaking card game that functions more as a simulation of scientific discovery than a traditional trick-taking or shedding game. Invented by Robert Abbott in 1956, it is a game of inductive reasoning where the rules of play are not known at the start. One player, acting as 'God' or 'Nature', secretly writes down a mathematical or logical rule governing which cards may follow others. The remaining players must intuit this rule through trial and errorâ€”observing which of their plays are accepted as 'legal' or rejected as 'illegal'â€”effectively practicing the scientific method to empty their hands.

Eleusis was created by Robert Abbott, a mathematician and puzzle designer. It first gained international fame when it was featured in Martin Gardner's 'Mathematical Games' column in Scientific American (June 1959).
4 to 8 players. One player is designated as 'God' (The Dealer) for the round.
Two standard 52-card decks mixed together (104 cards total).
Two standard 52-card decks mixed together (104 cards total).
God deals 12 cards to each player. One card is placed face-up in the center to start the 'Main Line'.

items.text: Eleusis Express: Streamlined version: 12 cards each, no Prophet; players may guess the rule aloud on a valid play. No-play incorrect call costs 1 penalty card; correct call replaces hand with one fewer card. Scoring: 12 minus cards in hand, plus 6 for correct guess, plus 3 for emptying hand.

The New Eleusis: Version with Prophet: 14 cards dealt to each non-dealer; player may become Prophet after valid play to judge moves; white and black markers every tenth card; elimination after fourth marker.
